claim: PstS precursor carries a cleaved signal peptide; mature protein is soluble
finding: N-termini of pre-PhoS and PhoS sequenced: 25-aa N-terminal extension with signal-peptide character; mature PhoS 321 aa, MW 34,422, no disulfide, no Met
context: E. coli K-12, purified protein chemistry
confidence: High. Direct protein sequencing of both precursor and mature forms. Does not itself test for a lipid anchor.

claim: PstS is periplasmic and made as a precursor
finding: phoS described as the structural gene for the periplasmic phosphate-binding protein; precursor has a 25-residue N-terminal signal sequence; mature 321 aa, MW 34,427
confidence: High. Basis of the EcoCyc IDA annotation to GO:0030288.

claim: The 25/26 cleavage site is used in vivo in wild-type cells
finding: Mature N-terminus of PstS observed as residues 26-37 (EASLTGAGATFP); this is the ECO:0000269 basis of UniProt SIGNAL 1..25
confidence: High for the cleavage site. Proteome-scale, not a dedicated fractionation study.

claim: PstS is a soluble periplasmic receptor
finding: 1.7 A structure of the liganded phosphate-binding protein; explicitly placed in the family of periplasmic receptors for osmotic-shock-sensitive transport systems
context: E. coli PBP crystallised as a soluble protein
confidence: High. Crystallised without detergent; covers mature 26-346 only.

claim: No structure contains the signal peptide or a membrane-embedded region
finding: All 13 X-ray entries map to UniProt P0AG82 residues 26-346 only (checked via RCSB polymer_entity_align)
confidence: High for what was crystallised. Absence from a crystal is not proof of absence in vivo.

claim: PstS associates with the inner-membrane transporter without being anchored
finding: PstS chain E modelled as 321 residues in mature numbering, docked on the periplasmic face; PstA (9-296) and PstC (14-319) carry the TM segments
context: E. coli PstSCAB complex, 2.7 and 2.9 A cryo-EM
confidence: High. Shows a transient complex interaction, which is the correct basis for a complex term, not for an intrinsic membrane term.

claim: Does the reference cited for GO:0016020 say PstS is at a membrane?
finding: No. It states PstC, PstB and PhoU are peripheral membrane proteins and PstA is an integral membrane protein. PstS is not listed.
context: E. coli pst region sequencing and gene-polypeptide assignment
confidence: High. Directly readable from the abstract; the NAS annotation is not supported for this subunit.

claim: Signal peptide present, transmembrane helices absent
finding: TM = 0, SP = Y, topology n6-17c25/26o (cleavage after residue 25)
confidence: High. Independent HMM; agrees with the experimentally determined site.

claim: No hydrophobic stretch long enough for a TM helix in the mature chain
finding: Mature 26-346 max 1.511; zero residues above the 1.6 threshold; only peak in the precursor is residue 16 (1.716), inside the signal peptide; longest w=9 run >1.6 in mature region is 9 residues
confidence: Moderate-high. Threshold-dependent, which is why the GRAVY benchmark below was added.

citation: This work: lipobox and Cys scan
finding: No [LVIAMFGT]-X-[GAS]-C lipobox in the first 40 residues; +1 residue is Glu26; zero cysteines in the whole 346-aa precursor
confidence: High. Zero Cys makes a thioether-linked diacylglyceryl anchor chemically impossible.

claim: The predicted cleavage site reproduces the published mature-protein data
finding: Residues 26-346 give 321 aa, 34,422 Da, 0 Met, 0 Cys; Magota reported 321 aa, 34,422 Da, no Met, no disulfide. Met18 lies inside the signal peptide, so an alternative site would break the zero-Met result.
context: Sequence analysis against published protein chemistry
confidence: High. Exact agreement on four independent values.

claim: Bulk composition of the mature chain is that of a soluble periplasmic protein
finding: Mature PstS GRAVY -0.332; 188 E. coli periplasmic mature chains median -0.385 (62nd percentile for PstS); 394 TM-annotated proteins median +0.511; Mann-Whitney p=1.8e-56; only 10.2% of TM proteins are less hydrophobic than PstS
context: UniProt reviewed E. coli K-12 reference sets
confidence: Moderate-high. Threshold-free, but composition is a proxy, not a localization assay.

claim: Could a membrane term reach E. coli PstS by ortholog transfer?
finding: 12/12 reviewed Actinomycetota PstS entries are +1-Cys lipoproteins annotated Cell membrane; 0/7 Pseudomonadota entries are (+1 = E,E,N,T,I,I,A), all annotated Periplasm. Fisher exact p=1.98e-05.
context: All 20 reviewed UniProt members of the PstS family
confidence: High for the pattern. Reviewed entries only (n=20), so the split is not a random sample of the family.

claim: Curated record contains no membrane feature
finding: SIGNAL 1..25 (ECO:0000269 PMID:9298646), CHAIN 26..346, subcellular location Periplasm, keywords Periplasm and Signal; no Transmembrane and no Lipidation feature anywhere in the entry
confidence: Database-level orientation, consistent with the primary data above.
